inline_comments.comment:
`useHtmlLabels` is passed as the fifth argument to `createLabel`, which maps to the `addBackground` parameter (signature: `createLabel(_vertexText, style, isTitle, isNode, addBackground = false, width)`). These are semantically unrelated: `addBackground` controls whether the `labelBkg` CSS class is added to the label container. When HTML labels are enabled (`useHtmlLabels = true`), all four edge terminal labels (`startLabelLeft`, `startLabelRight`, `endLabelLeft`, `endLabelRight`) will incorrectly receive that background class, causing an unintended visual change. Each call site should pass `false` here:

```js
await createLabel(
  edge.startLabelLeft,
  getLabelStyles(edge.labelStyle),
  undefined,
  false,
  false,   // addBackground, not useHtmlLabels
  width
);
```
All four call sites in this file have the same bug.

The original code used `log.debug('vertexText' + vertexText)` but this was changed to `log.info(...)`. The project convention for rendering code is `log.debug()` or `log.trace()` for diagnostic output; `log.info` is intended for higher-signal, user-visible messages. Please revert to `log.debug`. Additionally, prefer a template literal: `` log.debug(`vertexText ${vertexText}`) ``.

The previous implementation called `await replaceIconSubstring(decodeEntities(vertexText))`, which resolves icons via `mermaid.registerIconPacks()` and renders them as inline SVG. The replacement is a simple synchronous regex that only produces `<i class='...'>` HTML tags, which rely on FontAwesome CSS being present and do not support custom registered icon packs at all. This is a functional regression: any diagram using this code path (dagre-wrapper) with custom icon packs will silently render plain class-based `<i>` tags instead of SVG icons. If the intent is to unify behavior with `rendering-util/rendering-elements/createLabel.js` (which also uses the inline regex), this trade-off should be explicitly documented and a follow-up ticket opened to bring proper icon-pack support to both paths.

`DEFAULT_WRAPPING_WIDTH = 200` and the `getWrappingWidth()` helper (lines ~16–19) are now duplicated verbatim in `packages/mermaid/src/dagre-wrapper/createLabel.js`. The PR's stated goal is to reduce duplication, but this introduces new duplication. Both constants and helpers should be extracted to a single shared utility (e.g., `rendering-util/labelUtils.js`) and imported by both `createLabel` files.

The `padding-right: 1px` style that existed in the previous `addHtmlLabel` implementation was silently removed. The accompanying comment ('Fix for firefox') suggests it was a workaround for a layout bug in Firefox. If the fix is no longer needed, explain why in a comment. If it was accidentally dropped, restore it. Silent removal of browser-workaround styles makes future debugging much harder.

The changeset is marked `patch`, but this PR adds new user-visible features to labels that previously lacked them: KaTeX rendering, icon-pack support, text wrapping, and changed line-height/text-alignment. Per project conventions, new additive capabilities are a `minor` bump. A `patch` entry is appropriate only for pure bug fixes with no observable behavior change.

This file lives under `docs/`, which is auto-generated from the source tree by the docs-build pipeline. Project rules require that all documentation changes be made exclusively in the source; the generated `docs/` output must not be edited directly. The corresponding source change in `packages/mermaid/src/config.ts` is correct — remove this direct edit to `docs/` and let the pipeline regenerate it.

general_comments.comment: The `addHtmlLabel` function is now nearly identical in both `packages/mermaid/src/rendering-util/rendering-elements/createLabel.js` and `packages/mermaid/src/dagre-wrapper/createLabel.js` — same parameters, same KaTeX/sanitize logic, same temp-SVG measurement pattern, same wrapping check. The PR's stated goal is to reduce duplication, but it introduces a new, substantial duplicate instead. Since `dagre-wrapper/createLabel.js` is already marked `@deprecated`, the most practical fix is to have it import and re-export the implementation from `rendering-util/rendering-elements/createLabel.js` rather than maintaining a parallel copy.

The changeset description reads "fix: Refactor shared label rendering logic across diagrams, with no markdown-specific changes." This is inaccurate on two counts: (1) the PR does introduce behavior changes (KaTeX support, icon rendering, wrapping, line-height, text-align) that go beyond a pure refactor; and (2) "with no markdown-specific changes" is misleading given that the HTML-label path now processes KaTeX and icon patterns. The description should accurately state what observable behavior changes users can expect.
